notes.content: The page names Multomb(F) the grande multiombre, or M-multiombre, and states that it is a set-theoretic figure in M, faithfully indexed by the deployment tilde F, whose knowledge determines F. It then uses L hooked into M and inverse images to obtain (1.9): F-family to P(L), F mapped to omb(F), and F-family to Fig(L), F mapped to multomb(F). The text explicitly declines to expect injectivity of the first map and gives only a tendency toward injectivity for the second. It names omb(F) the petite ombre, or ombre when confusion seems excluded, and multomb the (petite) multiombre.
math_reading_decisions: The doubled F is kept literally; the ordinary F suggested by the surrounding sentence does not replace two visible stems.

The inverse-image Fig arrow has only an upper barb. Both (1.9) maps retain their cancelled injection hooks. The qualified injectivity language prompted attention to the hooks; it did not settle their shapes.
The P and domain-F alphabets remain uncertain at their first occurrences. Ordinary F, doubled F and the domain family are kept distinct.
The t in displayed multomb has a surviving stem and cross-stroke under dense ink; live/retraced and deleted states remain explicit alternatives. No prior letter is reconstructed.
The barred m in de barred-m pour is a verbal abbreviation, not an equality sign. It is not expanded in the transcription.

“quand une confusion semble exclue” qualifies use of the shorter name ombre.
